Uses normal terrain saving and network ownership, checks wards and the game's height limits, preserves ground paint, and edits only terrain-grid vertices inside the convex boundary. The visible edge follows the terrain's triangles. Costs one hoe use per polygon, with no stone cost.

Undo restores original heights and smoothing without refunding the hoe use. It refuses conflicting edits and checks current ward permissions and distance. Undo history lasts ten minutes, clears on reload, and requires the original terrain owner to remain available. An interrupted undo can be retried. Only leveling done with this version can be undone.

The fitted plane minimizes squared vertical height changes over the selected ground vertices, counting tile seams once. Polygons too narrow to define a plane are rejected. Install 0.1.3 or newer on the host and participating players for Shift + L in multiplayer. Markers are local previews and disappear on reload. Changes to the ground persist normally. Gameplay and multiplayer still need an in-game playtest.
mods.notes: 0.1.3: Shift + L flattens the current ground to a least-squares fitted plane, preserving its average slope. L still levels horizontally to the first marker. Tile seams count once in the fit, the outline shows the fitted plane, normal terrain limits are checked for every target height, and U undoes either action. Multiplayer owners need 0.1.3 for fitted planes.

mods.name: Shieldwall
mods.description:
A game within the game: build a Warstone, raise towers with war staves around it, and hold the line when a horde comes for it.

The Warstone (hammer, misc; 30 stone, 10 wood, 5 flint, 5 resin, near a workbench) is a standing stone that wards your home: a split, iron-bound menhir cut with war runes and a mark for each siege it holds. Everyone within 40 metres gets faster health and stamina regeneration, and with each siege the stone holds (its marks), carry weight, eitr regeneration and armor. Set it under a roof with a fire burning within 10 metres and the ward is twice as strong and adds comfort. One Warstone to a home.

Raise the stone's level (1 to 5) by building its upgrades within 10 metres: a war banner, a trophy totem, a horned brazier and a rune obelisk, each paid in warshards. The level decides how many war staves the stone can feed (2 to 10), how far (26 to 50 metres), which staves it can craft and how strong they can be made.

War staves are huge relics, too heavy to wield. Set them in stave sockets, stone pedestals you build on the ground, on walls or on top of towers, at least 5 metres apart. Use a socket to open its slot and choose the stave (the game's own chest window), Shift+Use to strengthen it in place with warshards. Staves fire on raiders and monsters in reach, aim at whoever is closest to the stone, count their kills, and never hurt players, companions, tames or buildings:
Ember stave (level 1): fireballs that splash.
Frost stave (level 2): a fast stream of ice shards that chill.
Hearth stave (level 2): mends you, your companions, your tames and, in a siege, the stone.
Thunder stave (level 3): heavy bolts at the strongest foe in 42 metres.
Blast stave (level 4): bombs that burst over the crowd.
Any other staff that throws something can be set in a socket too, weakly.

Shift+E on the stone sounds its war horn. A rift opens 60 to 95 metres away and a horde gathers, the strongest your world has unlocked: greydwarfs at first, then the Black Forest's host, the drowned dead, a mountain pack, a Fuling warband, the swarm of the mist and the Charred legion. After 90 seconds it marches on the stone in four to eight waves, ending with a warchief. A glowing line shows the road it will take and bends as you build: walls turn it aside, and where the road is shut a red line marks where they will break through. They fight what stands close, smash what blocks the way, and strike the stone when they reach it. Sappers go for your towers and tear down what holds them up, a raider a stave keeps hitting may turn on its tower, warchiefs strike buildings half again as hard, bats, drakes, deathsquitos and gjall fly over the walls, and diggers raise ramps over moats and dig at the stone's foot: undermine a Warstone (or dig your moat too close) and it topples, cracks and loses a mark. The game's own boss bar counts the waves and the stone's strength, with the game's raid music; the stone names what the next wave holds, and its horn can call the next wave early for bonus warshards.

Hold until the last of them falls and spoils appear by the stone: a chest of that land with warshards, coins and materials. Each siege held adds a mark: the ward grows and the horde grows. If they break the stone it cracks: its ward weakens until it holds a siege again. Nothing is lost; a fallen tower's stave lies where it stood. The first siege is fought by hand: the horde's warshards teach you the staves.

Once you have a Warstone, a base raid that would hit near it becomes a siege at the stone instead, with three minutes' warning (needs Shieldwall on the host).

Sieges run on the game of the player nearest the stone, so they work on a dedicated server without the mod; everyone who joins in needs Shieldwall. Warnings, wave pacing, the most raiders at once, the time limit and the horn's cooldown are in F7.
mods.notes: 0.4.26: The Warstone upgrades' bakes are fixed: the horned brazier's stone slab is a slab again (it had folded into a wedge), and the trophy totem's horns keep their shape and their lashings (they had crumpled). The war staves are re-baked with the same care.
mods.restart: The new models for the staves and the Warstone's upgrades show after restarting Valheim (a hot reload in a world leaves the hammer's build menu broken until then).

mods.name: Spyglass
mods.description:
A bronze spyglass. Craft it at the forge from 3 bronze. While it is in your inventory, Shift+Z raises it to your eye; Shift+Z or Escape lowers it.

Looking through it narrows the view to 4× optical magnification. The mouse wheel changes it from 2× to 8×, mouse turning slows to match, and a round eyepiece darkens the edges of the screen. The view is from your eyes, so your character never blocks it. You can still walk while looking.

Where you gaze, your map fills in a little: every quarter second, a 30-metre circle around the point you look at is uncovered, up to 600 metres away. The gaze stops at loaded buildings, trees and ground, and beyond them at the world's generated terrain or sea level. Looking at the sky uncovers nothing. Uncovered map is saved with your character like normal exploring. The distance to the point you gaze at shows under the eyepiece, and a middle click pins that point on your map; Shift+middle click lays a waypoint on your Wayfinder course instead, when Wayfinder is installed. From a ship's masthead, or anywhere you sit high above the water, the glass reaches 60% farther. Radius, range, magnification and the eyepiece can be changed in F7.

Shift+Z takes priority over a plain Z from other mods' shortcut helpers, such as GearSlots' quick slot 1, only while Shift is held. The spyglass is closed by opening the inventory, map, menu or chat, by dying, or by losing the item.

Only the player using it needs the mod for looking and crafting. A spyglass dropped on the ground is a world object: the host and nearby players need the mod too, or a host without it deletes it when its area loads. Removing the mod removes spyglasses from saved inventories. Compiled and checked against the local game; the model, icon, view, map reveal and GearSlots interaction still need in-game playtests.
mods.notes: 0.2.0: A rangefinder: the distance to the point you gaze at shows under the eyepiece. Middle click (Controls/Mark) pins that point on your map; with Shift it lays a waypoint on your Wayfinder course instead, when Wayfinder is installed. From a ship's masthead, or anywhere you sit high above the water, the glass uncovers the map 60% farther.

mods.name: TrophyHall
mods.description:
Hang your trophies and your hall remembers what you have slain.

Creature trophies on item stands you have built inside a base give everyone in that base small themed perks, shown as a Trophy hall status effect that stays with you for 30 minutes after you leave (adjustable), and never shrinks while it lasts. Each kind counts once, however many heads you hang:

Trolls: +30 carry weight. Draugr: slight poison resistance. Wolves: +10% stamina regeneration. Necks and serpents: +10% swim speed. Greydwarfs: +10% woodcutting skill gain. Boars: +10% health regeneration. Deer: +5% movement speed.

At most six perks apply, rarest first. Every kind of trophy also counts toward comfort under a roof: four kinds add +1, eight add +2. Walking into a hall names it after the ward's owner, counts its trophies and lists the creatures fallen there (once per hall, and again only when it has more trophies). Boss trophies stay on their altars, where the game uses them for Forsaken powers.

The perks are deliberately small: flavour felt over time, not a change to combat balance. Only the player in the hall needs the mod; it reads the item stands everyone already sees. Range, readings and the whole mod can be changed in F7.
mods.notes:
0.1.4: The hall's reading (its name, trophies and fallen creatures) no longer pops up every time you come near. Each hall is read out once, and again only when it has more trophies than before; your character remembers which halls you've seen, so a restart doesn't bring it back. Before, it came back every ten minutes, and sooner as you walked about the base.

0.1.3: The perks no longer shrink or vanish as you walk away. Before, the hall was re-read every two seconds from the trophies within 40 m of you, so heading for the door dropped perks one by one, and the whole effect went if the last heads in reach gave none. Now the effect you carry only grows while it lasts (trophies from another hall are added, up to six perks), stays full while you are near any themed trophy in a base, and counts down its 30 minutes once you leave.

0.1.2: The hall's perks stay with you after you leave: 30 minutes by default (LingerMinutes in F7, 0 for the old behaviour), counted down on the status bar and kept full while you are in the hall. Comfort still needs the hall's roof.

mods.name: Wayfinder
mods.description:
A navigator's kit for the northern seas: plotted courses, a sun-compass and sunstone, a sounding line, a weather-foretelling primstav, Flóki's ravens, ship names and fittings, beacon fires, sea-marks and a weather vane.

Plotted course: open the big map and hold Ctrl. Click to lay a waypoint. Click on a pin and the waypoint takes the pin's name; click on a leg and it goes into that leg. Ctrl+right-click lifts a waypoint, Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+R turns the course round for the way home, and Ctrl+Backspace clears it. The course is drawn on both maps as a dashed line, with a fainter line from you to the next waypoint. Under the compass, the navigator's notes give the next waypoint's distance and bearing, the distance left and the time left at your speed, and the wind for this leg: fair, on the quarter, on the beam, or a headwind, with the sail's pull as the game reckons it. Reaching a waypoint (40 m) moves on to the next, and cutting a corner to a later one counts. Each character keeps one course per world. Writing your map at a cartography table leaves your course there too, and reading the table takes it. While you steer, everyone aboard sees your course in blue.

Sun-Compass (workbench: 2 fine wood, 2 resin): a notched bearing-dial like the Uunartoq disc. Carry it and a compass band runs across the top of the screen, with your heading and marks for the next waypoint, home (your bed) and your raven's flight. It reads the sun by day and the lodestar by night. Cloud, rain and mist hide the sun, and the band drifts into dead reckoning.
Sunstone (workbench: 1 crystal, 1 leather scraps): a sólarsteinn of clear spar. It finds the sun through cloud and mist, so the compass stays true by day in any weather. It does not help at night.
Sounding Line (workbench: 2 stone, 4 leather scraps): aboard a ship it is cast ahead of the bow every few seconds. You get the depth in fathoms where she will be, what the bottom is (sand, mud, rock, shell), a shout when the water shoals, and a note when you are over the deep sea, where the serpents are.
Primstav (workbench: 1 fine wood, 1 coal): the game draws its weather from the clock, so the stave tells truly what comes next and when: "Clear skies; rain in 3:20". When the next waypoint lies in another land, it also gives that land's weather. A raid, a boss or Moder's power can still bring its own weather.
Caged Raven (workbench: 2 wood, 3 feathers, 1 raw meat): use it to let the raven go. It climbs, circles, and flies for the nearest land it sees, unexplored land first. Your map keeps a line the way it flew, and the land where it was heading is drawn in. If it sees no land within 2 km it comes back to you. Only you see your raven.

Ships: every ship has a name, a kenning or a famous ship's name until you give her your own at the helm with Shift+E. Each ship you have sailed in is pinned on your map by name, so you never lose your boat. Taking the pin off the map forgets her. Masts carry a lantern, lit from dusk till dawn, and a gilded vane at the masthead that swings to the wind. Shift+E at the mast climbs to the lookout's seat, a board lashed under the masthead: up there the map fills in wider around you, the higher the seat the wider (three times as wide from a drakkar's), and a spyglass reaches farther.

Building (hammer): Weather Vane (1 bronze, 2 fine wood), a gilded veðurviti on a pole that swings to the wind; look at it for the wind and the weather to come. Beacon Fire (12 wood, 12 stone, 6 resin), the game's bonfire lifted onto a timber tower with an iron basket. Fed with wood, it burns with a glow seen from far out at sea. Shift+E names it, and everyone who has seen it keeps it on their map. Sea-Mark (4 wood, 2 resin), a floating spar-buoy with a birch-withy topmark and a little lamp that burns at night. Place it on water; name it (E) and it goes on your map.

Everything is in F7 → Mod settings. Players need the mod to see the course, compass and notes. The host and nearby players need it for the built pieces, items on the ground, ship names and the helm's course; a host without it deletes those objects. Removing the mod removes its items from inventories. Live-checked: course plotting and map lines, compass band, notes, forecast against the game's weather, raven, piece and ship models, the lead aboard, ship naming, and the masthead climb and descent. Not yet played: under way at sea, ship pins, helm sharing with a second player, the cartography table, and building the pieces by hand.
mods.notes: 0.1.10: The primstav shows the next feast-day within a fortnight under its forecast (Jarldom's festivals: Sigrblot, Midsummer, Winter Nights, Yule). Api v2: AddFeastDay, ClearFeastDays. Test tool: wayfinder feast [name days].

mods.name: Bob's Animations
mods.description:
An animation pack for other mods: keyframed clips played over a character's own animation, a bone at a time, so a villager sitting in a chair keeps sitting while their arm lifts a tankard to their lips. No asset bundles: clips are made in Blender over a skeleton captured from the game and shipped as small files inside the mod.

Seated clips: sit_drink (a long pull from a tankard), sit_toast_left/right (raised toward someone, then a pull), sit_talk_left/right (open-handed beats toward a neighbour, head turned, jaw working), sit_point_left/right, sit_laugh (slapping the knee, doubled over), sit_think (a fist under the chin, stroking the beard), sit_cheer (both fists pumped), sit_board_move (a piece moved on the table in front), and two loops, sit_fold_arms and sit_elbows (leaning forward, elbows on the knees). A seated clip blends out by itself when its character gets up.

Standing clips: stand_fish (the rod held out, a loop), stand_fish_cast, stand_fish_reel (a fish taken off the line and held up), walk_carry (an armful carried while walking, the item given when played), stand_sow and stand_harvest (crouched, feet planted), stand_watch (a hand over the eyes, looking about), stand_drum (a loop) and stand_recite. A standing clip ends by itself when its character walks off; one clip after another blends without a snap.

For modders: Anim.Play(character, "sit_drink"), Anim.Play(character, "walk_carry", "Wood"), Anim.Stop(character), Anim.Playing(character); Clip.Register(json) adds your own clips. The game that runs a character starts and stops its clip; what plays and since when is kept on the character's network object, so everyone near sees the same, in step. A clip blends in and out over the game's pose, and can put an item (a tankard) in a hand while it plays.

Install it on every player who should see the animations (and on the game that runs the characters). Native Linux and Windows.
mods.notes: 0.3.7: an armful carried while walking ends once the villager stands still (it could outlast the walk when they were called away).

mods.name: Respite
mods.description:
A breath between raids, and time to get in position.

One raid clock for the world. After a raid, the land near it rests: no other raid comes within 500 m for 1.5 in-game days, and no place gets more than three in seven days. The clock counts the game's own raids and the raids of Bob's other mods, so they no longer pile up: Omens' bad omens wait their turn (or fade), Jarldom's draugr warbands wait another night and the Fulings put off their next demand, and a Shieldwall horn starts the clock like any raid. Bases farther apart keep their own clocks.

Raiders gather outside the base before they come. A spot past your farthest building is chosen on open ground outside every ward; everyone near is told where ("They gather to the north-east, 120 m out: 90 seconds."), it is pinned on the map, and a rift churns there. When the warning is up they come from there. The game's raids muster too: no spawns for the warning, then they come from the gathering spot (or at least from well outside the base), and they last the warning longer so it doesn't eat the fight.

Cooldown, area, weekly cap, warning, and how far out they gather are all in F7. The host's game keeps the clock (saved per world) and its settings count; players' games keep a copy, so a mod deciding on a player's game asks the same clock. On a vanilla dedicated server each player's game keeps its own clock for the session.
mods.notes: 0.1.1: A Claude Tools test command, respite: status, raid, roll, stop, muster and clear (forget the raids near a place).

mods.name: Wrong Universe
mods.description:
Somebody's sci-fi kit fell through a crack into the tenth world. None of it belongs here, and all of it works. Made at the forge (the speeder with the hammer); every number and cost is a setting.

Laser Pistol: one-handed, red bolts, one per click, overheats if you lean on it. Laser Rifle: two-handed; hold attack to charge, release to fire a blue beam out to 260 m; a full charge burns through four bodies; hold block to shoulder it and zoom. The pistol is held in one hand, Han Solo style; the rifle is shouldered and sighted down the barrel. Both point at what the crosshair is on, kick, and vent when overheated.
Laser Sword: the game's sword swings with a glowing blade that hums louder the faster it moves, ignites when drawn, chops trees and breaks rock. Blue, green, red, violet, yellow, white or cyan.
Jetpack (utility slot): jump, then hold Jump to fly; move keys steer, Run boosts. Fuel refills on the ground. No fall damage while you wear it. Everyone sees the flames.
Infrared Goggles (helmet): thermal view. The world goes dim and blue, and every warm body within 80 m glows through walls and hills; you see at night. H switches them.
Combat Drone: use it to launch a drone that circles your shoulder and zaps enemies that mean harm; use it again to call it home. Its battery recharges in your bag. One drone per item.
Orbital Uplink: point at the ground up to 300 m away and paint it. Three seconds later a low orbit ion cannon puts a pillar of light there: 600 damage over 12 m, fells trees, breaks rocks, sets things burning and digs a crater. 60 s to recharge. Spares buildings, and digs no crater near a ward or your builds unless you allow it.
Hover Speeder (hammer, near a forge): rides 1 m over land and water. W/S throttle, A/D steer, Shift boost, Jump hops; a friend can ride pillion. Rams enemies at speed.
Gravity Gun: hold attack to lift a creature, log, cart or loose item and carry it; block flings it. Flung things hurt what they hit.
Displacer: blink to the crosshair, up to 60 m, every 3 s.
Stim Pack: full health and stamina now, then 30 s of six times the regeneration and 40% more speed.
Recall Beacon: one use, takes you to your bed, ore and all.

Friends are never hurt (tamed animals; other players only with PvP on both sides). Everything is seen and heard by other players. Native Linux and Windows.
mods.notes: 0.2.10: The Displacer can jump anywhere on the map: switch on DisplacerMapJump (section 8 - Gadgets), then its secondary attack opens the map and a click jumps you there, landing on the ground, the sea, or the floor of whatever is built there (the world loads around you as through a portal). The cooldown still applies. Its other settings, DisplacerRange and DisplacerCooldown, are in the same section. New test command: wu gadget map.
mods.restart: Adds saved items with recipes and a build piece. Install Wrong Universe on the host and every player, then restart Valheim before loading the world.

mods.name: Godforged
mods.description:
The gods' own treasures. Made at the forge; every cost is a setting.

Mjölnir: Thor's hammer, one-handed, with lightning in every blow and a short handle (a fly bit the smith). Throw it (secondary attack) and it tumbles humming through the air, lightning strikes where it lands (and splits trees), and it flies back to your hand, hitting what's in its way. Only a hand in Járngreipr can throw it; bare, it burns.
Járngreipr: Thor's iron gauntlets, worn in the trinket slot: splinted iron vambraces and iron-plated leather gloves, made to fit your own hands.
Gungnir: Odin's spear, a dwarf's work with a huge angular head. Throw it and, with a rush of wind, it finds the foe you look at, turning in flight to reach it, then comes back to your hand.
Draupnir: Odin's ring. Carry it, and every ninth dawn it drips eight rings' worth of coins.
Brísingamen: Freyja's necklace. Carry it, and when you're healed, friends near you are healed too.
Gjallarhorn: Heimdall's horn. Blow it, and everyone hears it and sees where you stand; those beside you take heart.
Thor's kit: Mjölnir, Járngreipr and the game's own Megingjord together, and the lightning leaps from foe to foe.

A thrown relic is never lost: if it can't come home (you fell, your bag is full) it drops where it is. Everyone sees the throw, the return and the lightning. Native Linux and Windows.
mods.notes: 0.3.2: Three more relics. Draupnir (Odin's ring, carried): every ninth dawn it drips eight rings' worth of coins. Brísingamen (Freyja's necklace, carried): when you're healed (not food regeneration), friends within 20 m are healed half as much, with a golden glint. Gjallarhorn (Heimdall's horn, used): everyone in the world hears it and sees a ping where you stand; friends within 30 m take Heimdall's Watch (a minute of quicker stamina); then it rests five minutes. Api 2: OnDrip, OnHorn.
mods.restart: Adds saved items with recipes and networked projectiles. Install Godforged on the host and every player, then restart Valheim before loading the world.

mods.name: Byre
mods.description:
Livestock for the long houses: sheep in the Meadows and goats in the Mountains, to tame, breed, shear and milk.

Wild herds: sheep graze in small herds (two to four) on open Meadows away from the trees, goats on steep Mountain slopes. They're shy: they run from you when you come within 8 m (goats 10 m), half that if you crouch. Hurt one and it runs. They never fight back.

Taming: as with boars. Drop what they eat and stay back; a fed animal calms and tames in time (sheep about 20 minutes, goats 30). Sheep eat dandelions, berries, carrots, turnips, barley and cloudberries; goats all that and thistle and onions too.

Breeding: a fed, tame pair has young (lambs and kids) now and then, up to six of a kind close together. The young grow up in under two days and come tame.

Shears (forge, 3 copper): carry them and press E on a tame sheep in full fleece. It drops 2 or 3 wool, 1 if it was hungry. The wool grows back in two days, twice as long if it's kept hungry. Look at a sheep to see how long it has to go.

Milk pail (workbench, 6 wood): carry it and press E on a tame goat. It gives a jug or two of goat's milk once a day (one, and every two days, if hungry). Goat's milk is food: a little health, good stamina.

Feeding trough (workbench, 10 wood): put food in it, and hungry tame animals within 12 m walk over and eat from it, one bite at a time, each its own food. Boars, wolves and the other tames use it too.

Settings (decided by the server in multiplayer): wild herds on or off, how often they come, how fast wool and milk come back, and what the shears, pail and trough cost.

Needs a restart to install or update: the animals, items and trough are saved in the world. Every player and the server need it.
mods.notes: 0.1.2: wild sheep and goats can be tamed near a colony: seeing villagers, tame wolves or a player far off no longer keeps them alerted (alerted, the game never tames them); only a player within about 16 m, or being hurt, does. Live-checked: shearing and milking, wool and milk growing back (a fed animal twice as fast, 2-3 wool to a hungry one's 1), tame animals eating from the trough, a fed goat pair in a pen bearing kids, wild herds spawning in the Meadows, taming progressing once a wild one has eaten. Test commands: byre bait (food at a wild one's feet), byre troughs fill, taming time left in byre herds.
mods.restart: Adds saved animals (sheep, goats and their young), items (wool, goat's milk, shears, milk pail) and a trough piece. Install Byre on the host or server and every player, then restart Valheim before loading the world.

mods.name: Homespun
mods.description:
Homespun cloth, from the field to the back. Flax and wool go through the steps they really went through, at stations you build at a workbench (Crafting tab), and come out as cloth and clothes.

Retting pool: a plank trough of water. Put flax in and it soaks for 45 seconds a bundle, the stalks rotting loose from the fibre: retted flax. Holds 40. 16 wood, 6 stone, 4 resin.

Flax brake: a hinged wooden jaw that breaks the retted stalks, with a hackle of iron teeth that combs the fibre straight: line flax, 10 seconds each. It combs a lox pelt into 4 wool, too. Holds 20. 12 wood, 10 iron nails.

Spinning: the game's spinning wheel spins line flax into 2 linen thread (raw flax still gives 1, as it always has) and wool into yarn. Or carry a drop spindle (workbench: 2 wood, 1 stone) and spin as you walk: hold it and it spins what's in your bag, line flax first, then wool, a thread or yarn every minute or so.

Warp-weighted loom: a frame leaned back, the warp hanging from it on stone weights. Weave a linen bolt (8 linen thread), a wool bolt (8 yarn) or 2 woven bands (2 thread, 2 yarn). 20 wood, 10 stone, 2 leather scraps.

Sewing table: cut and sew bolts into clothes. Linen undertunic, wool tunic, wool dress, wool trousers and a hooded wool cloak, in the colours of undyed linen and wool: light, warm work clothes, not armour. And Hildir's coloured clothes, made here from cloth (berries for the colour) instead of bought. 12 wood, 2 leather scraps, 1 bronze.

With Byre installed, its sheep's fleece spins straight into yarn, no lox pelt needed.

Dyeing comes later.
mods.notes: 0.1.1: retted flax is a sheaf of grey stalks tied round the middle, line flax a twisted golden strick. The five garments lie folded in their own looks (the undertunic pale linen, the tunic with its red band, the dress with its brooches and beads, the trousers with their drawstring, the cloak with its hood and ring-pin), and their icons are drawn from those. Worn, their pictures are recoloured to bleached linen or undyed wool. The stations' build icons and the items' icons are drawn again once you're in the world, in flat light (0.1.0's came out green or neon).
mods.restart: Adds saved items, recipes and pieces. Install Homespun on the host and every player, then restart Valheim before loading the world.
